claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions. Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I do have a child. I'm asking about my son Alex - he's 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you're inquiring about your son Alex, who is 8 years old.

Now I need to ask you a few more questions to assess your eligibility:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Now I need to understand your responsibility for Alex:

**Do you live with Alex, or if not, do you contribute at least the same amount as Child Benefit (or the equivalent in kind) towards his care - for example, on food, clothes, or pocket money?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect. A few more questions to complete the assessment:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Just a couple more questions:

**Is Alex in any of the following situations:**
- In hospital or residential accommodation for more than 12 weeks?
- In care (provided by the local council) for more than 8 weeks?
- Living with someone else?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, actually, Alex has been in hospital for a few months now - it's been quite difficult for us.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm sorry to hear that Alex has been in hospital - that must be very difficult for you and your family.

To help me assess how this affects your Child Benefit eligibility, I need to ask:

**How long has Alex been in hospital, and do you regularly spend money on him while he's there (for example, on clothes, toys, treats, or other items for him)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's been in hospital for about 15 weeks now. To be honest, I'm not sure if what I've been able to do counts as "regularly spending" - it's been a difficult time financially and emotionally.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand this is a very difficult time for you. Let me clarify what might count as regularly spending money on Alex.

According to the rules, spending on Alex could include things like:
- Clothes
- Toys or games
- Treats or snacks
- Books or entertainment
- Toiletries
- Any other items for his personal use

**Have you been able to purchase any items like these for Alex during the time he's been in hospital, even if infrequently or in small amounts?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I really don't know if what I've managed counts. Some weeks I can, some weeks I can't - it's been inconsistent and I'm honestly not sure how to answer that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I completely understand - it's a difficult situation and you're being honest about the uncertainty.

Let me ask one final question to make sure I have all the information:

**Is Alex in a UK hospital, and is there anything else about his situation or your circumstances that you think might be relevant to your Child Benefit claim?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he's in a UK hospital. I can't think of anything else that would be relevant - he's just my 8-year-old son who lives with me normally, but he's been in hospital for these past 15 weeks. No one else claims for him, and there's nothing else unusual about our situation.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me carefully consider your situation based on the rules:

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## Summary

Based on the information you've provided, I cannot make a definitive determination about your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex - your situation requires individual assessment by HMRC.

**Here's why:**

Under normal circumstances, you would clearly be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex because:
- He's 8 years old (under 16)
- You live in the UK
- He normally lives with you
- No one else is claiming for him

**However**, Alex has been in hospital for approximately 15 weeks, which is longer than the 12-week threshold. After 12 weeks in a UK hospital, Child Benefit usually stops, **but** there's an important exception: you can continue to receive Child Benefit if you're regularly spending money on Alex.

Since you're uncertain whether your spending pattern meets the "regularly spending" requirement, I cannot definitively say whether you're eligible or not.

**What I recommend:**

You should contact HMRC's Child Benefit Office directly to discuss your specific situation. They can:
- Assess whether your spending pattern qualifies as "regularly spending"
- Advise you on your ongoing entitlement
- Help ensure you receive any benefits you're entitled to

I hope Alex recovers soon, and I wish you and your family all the best during this difficult time.
